name: Cerium
occurrence: The most abundant rare-earth element overall, more common in Earth's crust than copper.
majorUses: Catalytic converter and diesel fuel additives
notableCharacteristics: One of the very few lanthanides with a stable and useful +4 oxidation state alongside the typical +3, thanks to the extra stability of an empty 4f subshell in Ce⁴⁺.
whyHere: Losing all four of its outer electrons (one 4f, one 5d, two 6s) leaves cerium with an empty, stable 4f⁰ configuration in the Ce⁴⁺ state, which is exactly why it — unlike most lanthanides — readily forms both +3 and +4 ions.
didYouKnow: Despite the 'rare earth' label, cerium is more abundant in Earth's crust than copper, lead, or tin — 'rare earth' historically referred to how hard these elements were to separate from each other, not how scarce they are.
genZNote: 'Rare earth' is a total misnomer, cerium's more common than copper. It's just a nightmare to separate from its neighbours.
